thesis: Sarah Tavel argues that dominant marketplaces often face disruption when they fail to aggressively expand their supply side, allowing new entrants to leapfrog them by introducing a different atomic unit of supply or a more favorable fee structure. She illustrates this pattern with the food delivery industry, where DoorDash and Uber Eats overtook Grubhub by bringing in third-party delivery drivers to onboard restaurants that the incumbent ignored, and with the travel industry, where Airbnb and Booking.com disrupted incumbents by changing the fundamental unit of supply or reducing fees to make listing economically viable for independent owners.
